t: The Pacific Marine Fisheries Commission constituted by the compact shall make an annual report to Congress not later than sixty days after the beginning of each regular session thereof.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an interstate compact commission (a body of states, outside the federal government) communicating with Congress counts as participation. But the section only imposes an annual reporting duty; it does not require or invite the federal government to consult the Commission before making any federal decision. A report to Congress with no tied federal decision, comment process, advisory role, or right to sue is not participation under the definition.
fable.s: shall make an annual report to Congress not later than sixty days after the beginning of each regular session thereof

qwen_block.w: This section requires a report to be submitted to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress or its committees.
qwen_block.s: The Pacific Marine Fisheries Commission constituted by the compact shall make an annual report to Congress not later than sixty days after the beginning of each regular session thereof.

opus.w: This section only requires an annual report to Congress, and the definition says reports to Congress are not participation. The Commission is an interstate compact body and therefore outside the federal government, but no federal agency is required or allowed to consult it before making a decision. It has no advisory, comment, hearing or litigation role here, so the outside-party reading fails.
opus.s: The Pacific Marine Fisheries Commission constituted by the compact shall make an annual report to Congress not later than sixty days after the beginning of each regular session thereof.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The Pacific Marine Fisheries Commission is an interstate compact body made up of state representatives, who are outside the federal government. Its required report could therefore look like outsiders taking part in federal decisions.

   **Why it fails:** The section only requires the Commission to send Congress an annual report. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory role or right to sue tied to any federal decision. Under the definition, reports to Congress are not participation.
